title: The Slow Postcard
premise: Marguerite Fairweather ghostwrote the memoirs of Julian Ashcombe, the rival publisher who once loved her—and whom she betrayed a decade ago to protect her own career. Stranded together in a snowbound Vermont inn while a hostile takeover threatens both their houses, they are forced to confront the postcard she never sent, the truth she buried, and the loyalty that cost them everything. As the storm traps them with the wreckage of their twenties, Marguerite must choose between the safe invisibility she built and the truth that could save Julian's company—and expose her own. In the end, she publishes the confession under her own name, forgives herself, and chooses love not as an escape from duty but as its fulfillment.
about_author: Emrys Villalobos is a former small-press editor who spent seven years ghostwriting before publishing under their own name, a history that seeps into every page about borrowed voices and reclaimed ones. They write from a farmhouse in upstate New York, surrounded by unsent letters and a stubborn orange cat.

chapters.title: The Unsent Postcard
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Ten years after walking out of Julian Ashcombe's life, Marguerite ghostwrites memoirs in a borrowed voice, her own name fading from the industry. She finds an unsent postcard from her old life in a desk drawer. Beat: quiet unease—the past isn't finished with her.

chapters.title: A Voice for Hire
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her agency offers a lucrative contract: the memoirs of Julian's estranged business partner, Celeste Marr. Marguerite hesitates—Celeste's story will inevitably touch the betrayal she buried. She accepts, needing the money and the anonymity. Beat: complicity; she steps back into the fire for safety's sake.

chapters.title: Interviews with a Stranger
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Celeste, sharp and dying, dictates her memoirs with unsettling candor about a young editor she once destroyed—a story Marguerite recognizes as her own. Celeste seems to know who Marguerite is but says nothing. Beat: dread wrapped in flattery.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian, fighting a hostile takeover by Celeste's consortium, is summoned to a mediation weekend at a Vermont inn. He's told a neutral ghostwriter will document the settlement. He agrees, unaware the ghostwriter is Marguerite. Beat: duty over desire, again.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The storm closes the mountain pass hours after Marguerite, Julian, and Celeste arrive. The reveal happens over bad wine: Julian sees her, and the room goes silent. Celeste smiles faintly. Beat: shock, old wounds reopened with no exit.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Trapped, Marguerite narrates her decade of careful invisibility—pseudonyms, rented rooms, love deliberately unfollowed. Julian demands to know why she betrayed him to Celeste's old firm. She refuses to answer. Beat: defensiveness as armor cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian rereads the old acquisition ledger and realizes the numbers Marguerite was accused of leaking were falsified—by someone at Celeste's firm. Doubt creeps in. He confronts Celeste, who deflects elegantly. Beat: the first crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: The Power Outage
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The inn loses power; candles, cold, and proximity. Julian and Marguerite argue by firelight until the argument becomes confession-adjacent—almost touching, almost honest. Celeste watches from the stairs. Beat: intimacy rekindled under pressure, still armored.

chapters.title: Celeste's Terms
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Celeste privately offers Marguerite a deal: finish the memoirs omitting the falsified ledger, and Celeste will fund her independence forever. It's a bribe shaped like kindness. Marguerite wavers. Beat: power corrupting gently, the old temptation wearing new clothes.

chapters.title: The Second Night
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian and Marguerite talk until dawn—not about the betrayal but about who they were before it. He admits he built his company to prove something to her absence. She admits she never stopped reading his catalog. Beat: tenderness without absolution.

chapters.title: The Missing Chapter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reviewing Celeste's dictation tapes, Marguerite finds a deleted segment: Celeste's own admission that she framed Marguerite to poach her from Julian's firm. The proof is on tape—but exposing it destroys the memoir contract and Celeste's legacy. Beat: the truth in her hands, heavy as a stone.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Old Address
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite's mentor calls: her agency will blackball her if she breaks contract. Her loyalty to the people who sheltered her invisible years wars with loyalty to the truth—and to Julian. Beat: the cost of every loyalty made explicit.

chapters.title: The Mediation Table
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Roads partially clear; a video mediation proceeds. Julian, armed with the ledger discrepancy but not the tape, stalls the takeover. Celeste, ill and sharp, senses Marguerite knows something. Beat: public chess over private fault lines.

chapters.title: Confession at the Window
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite finally tells Julian the whole truth: she didn't leak the numbers—she stayed silent to protect her ailing mother's job at Celeste's firm, then let the lie calcify out of shame. Julian's fury is quiet and worse than shouting. Beat: the mirror moment—she forgives no one yet, least of all herself.

chapters.title: What Julian Buried
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confesses his own sin: he knew Marguerite's mother was ill and said nothing, letting her walk into the trap alone because his pride was wounded first. His betrayal was silence too. Beat: symmetry of guilt; the ground levels between them.

chapters.title: The Tape
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite plays Celeste the deleted tape segment, alone. Celeste doesn't deny it; she asks Marguerite what she'll do with it, testing whether power has already corrupted her the way it once corrupted Celeste. Beat: the thematic crucible—truth vs. leverage.

chapters.title: Deadline: The Takeover Vote
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The consortium moves the shareholder vote up—three days. Without proof of the falsified ledger, Julian loses his company. Marguerite holds the tape that could save him, but using it means torching her career and Celeste's dying wish. Beat: time running out, stakes fused.

chapters.title: Celeste's Last Draft
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Celeste, hospitalized by the storm's aftermath, dictates a final chapter to Marguerite: a full confession of the frame, to be published only if Marguerite chooses truth. 'A ghostwriter's last gift is a voice that isn't hers,' Celeste says. Beat: the antagonist's redemption, and her passing of the burden.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The night before the vote, Marguerite drafts two endings: the safe memoir, and the true one. She burns the safe draft in the inn's hearth, then calls Julian—not to save his company first, but to say she's sorry, decade-late. Beat: climax of character; the choice precedes the consequence.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At the shareholder meeting, Marguerite arrives and reads Celeste's confession aloud, authenticating it with the tape. The vote collapses; the takeover dies. Julian's company is saved by the woman the industry erased—and she signs her own name to the statement. Beat: external climax; love expressed as truth-telling.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Aftermath: the industry reels, the agency cuts her, and Marguerite discovers she doesn't mind. She begins writing her own book. Julian asks for nothing, only offers to be in the room while she writes it. Beat: falling action; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Slow Postcard
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A year later, Marguerite mails Julian the decade-old postcard at last, finally addressed and stamped, meeting him at the Vermont inn where the storm once trapped them. Forgiveness, like a postcard, traveled slowly—but it arrived. Beat: resolution; love against duty, resolved as duty fulfilled.
